actions.title: Perform Point-of-Care Glucose Test
actions.prompt: Indicate the step-by-step process to follow to safely and effectively perform a point-of-care glucose test in accordance with best-practice guidelines.
items: Power on the glucometer, check the expiration date and integrity of test strips, and insert a new test strip into the meter.
Select a lateral side of a fingertip, place the hand in a dependent position, clean the selected fingertip area with an alcohol wipe, and allow the selected fingertip area to dry completely.
Position the lancet within the cleaned fingertip area, activate the lancet to puncture the skin, dispose of used lancet immediately in sharps container.

Wipe away first drop of blood, gently squeeze finger proximal to puncture site to produce drop of blood, bring test strip in meter to the blood drop, allow capillary action to wick blood into test strip.
Apply clean gauze to puncture site with slight pressure to stop bleeding, then apply bandage to site as needed, and read glucometer results when displayed on meter and verbally share results.

Interpretation: Marked hyperglycemia; consistent with diabetes and risk of DKA

actions.title: Perform Urine Dipstick Test
actions.prompt: Indicate the step-by-step process to follow to safely and effectively perform a urine dipstick test in accordance with best-practice guidelines.
items: Obtain recently collected urine sample and verify urine sample is labelled correctly and matches patient identity, then check the expiration date and integrity of the urine dipstick test container/supplies and remove only one dipstick without touching the reagent pads

Gently swirl the urine container to resuspend any settled elements and then dip the reagent end of the test strip fully into the urine, ensure all pads are briefly but completely immersed, then remove the test strip and run the edge of the edge of the strip along the rim of the container to remove excess urine while keeping the strip horizontal

Keeping the strip horizontal, place the strip flat on a clean, absorbent surface with pads facing up and initiate timing immediately and wait specified time for each parameter as indicated on the test strip container, then read each test zone only during the correct timeframes, comparing reagent pad colors to the manufacturer's color chart in good lighting

title: Clinic Check-In and Chief Concern
description: Practice greeting a patient, verifying identity with two approved identifiers, using open-ended communication to identify the reason for today's visit, and documenting the patient's chief concern while maintaining professionalism, privacy, and patient-centered care.
learningObjective:
Use a professional greeting when beginning a patient encounter.  

Verify patient identity using two approved identifiers before discussing health information.  

Ask an open-ended question to determine the patient's chief concern.  

Accurately document the patient's stated reason for today's visit using the patient's own words whenever appropriate.

actions.title: Professional Introduction
actions.prompt: Select the best option of how you would professionally begin this patient encounter with Olivia Bennett? Then, if you haven’t already done so, talk to the patient using the best option selected.
items: "Good morning, Olivia. My name is Jordan, and I'm a Health Science student assisting with your clinic intake today. I'll ask you a few questions to get started. Is that okay?"
"Hi, what's your name and why are you here today?"
"Please tell me your date of birth so we can get this appointment started."
"Hey Olivia! Let's get this over with so we can move on to the next patient."
actions.correct: "Good morning, Olivia. My name is Jordan, and I'm a Health Science student assisting with your clinic intake today. I'll ask you a few questions to get started. Is that okay?"
actions.resultName: If you haven’t already done so, talk to the patient using the best option. The patient will respond verbally when spoken to.

actions.title: Verify Two Patient Identifiers
actions.prompt: Arrange the steps in the correct order to verify Olivia Bennett’s identity before discussing health information. Then, if you haven’t already done so, talk to the patient following the determined sequential order of the items.
items: Explain that you need to confirm identity before discussing health information.
Ask the patient to state her full name.
Ask the patient to state her date of birth.
Compare the stated name and DOB with the patient chart.
Confirm that the identifiers match before continuing the intake conversation.
actions.resultName: If you haven’t already done so, talk to the patient using the following the determined sequential order of the items. The patient will confirm identity when asked.

actions.title: Explain Identity Verification
actions.prompt: Identify which explanation best describes why you are verifying Olivia’s identity before continuing. Then, if you haven’t already done so, explain to the patient why verifying identity is important using the best option.
items: “We verify two identifiers to make sure we are speaking with the right person and protecting your private health information.”
“It is just something the computer makes us do before we can move on.”
“I need to check because patients sometimes give the wrong information.”
“We only need to do this if you are here for a serious medical problem.”
actions.correct: “We verify two identifiers to make sure we are speaking with the right person and protecting your private health information.”
actions.resultName: If you haven’t already done so, explain to the patient why you verify the patient’s identity using the best option. Patient will respond verbally when spoken to.

actions.title: Obtain Chief Complaint
actions.prompt: Select the best option of the following options to ask Olivia as an open-ended question to learn the reason for today’s visit. Then, if you haven’t already done so, talk to the patient using the best option selected and document the Chief Complaint in the patient chart.
items: "What brings you in for your visit today?"
"You're here for your annual physical today, right?"
"Are you here because you're sick?"
“What chief complaint would you like documented for today's encounter?"
